Recurring Payslip

Set up recurring payslips for regular employee payments.

Automatically generate payslips for salaries, wages, and regular compensation.

Next issue date

The date when the next payslip will be automatically created. This date advances automatically based on your pay cycle.

Set this to your next pay date. The system checks daily for payslips due to be created.

Interval

The frequency interval for creating payslips. This number works with the period type to match your pay cycle.

Common examples: 1 Week = weekly pay, 2 Weeks = fortnightly/bi-weekly pay, 1 Month = monthly salary.

PeriodType

The period type that works with the interval to determine frequency. Select the unit of time for your pay cycle.

Most businesses pay weekly, fortnightly, or monthly. Choose what matches your payroll schedule.

MonthDay

For monthly recurring payslips, specify which day of the month the payslip should be created.

Common choices are 'Last day of month' for month-end payroll or specific dates like the 15th or 25th.

Employee

Select the employee who will receive this recurring payslip. Each generated payslip will be linked to this employee.

Create separate recurring payslips for each employee, even if they have the same pay schedule.

Description

A description that identifies this recurring payslip and will be copied to each generated payslip.

Optional but helpful for identifying pay periods. Examples: 'Regular salary', 'Fortnightly wages', 'Monthly pay'.

Earnings

The earnings items to include in each payslip. These are amounts added to the employee's gross pay.

Add lines for regular wages, overtime, bonuses, allowances, or any other earnings. Each line can have different rates or fixed amounts.

For variable earnings like overtime hours, you'll need to edit individual payslips after creation.

Deductions

The deduction items to subtract from gross earnings. These reduce the employee's net pay.

Common deductions include income tax, social security, health insurance, retirement contributions, or loan repayments.

Deductions can be fixed amounts or calculated as percentages of earnings.

Contributions

The employer contribution items that don't affect the employee's net pay but represent additional employer costs.

These might include employer retirement contributions, employer-paid insurance, or payroll taxes paid by the employer.

Contributions appear on the payslip for transparency but don't reduce take-home pay.

Automatic reference

When enabled, the system automatically assigns sequential reference numbers to each generated payslip.

Recommended for maintaining organized payroll records. Reference numbers help track payments and resolve queries.
